heuristics.description: This is the initial knowledge base file. Every time a new compiler trick or C structure is discovered to match PS1/PsyQ assembly perfectly, an entry should be added here.

The .c files are compiled using tools/gcc-2.6.0-psx/cc1 (or 2.7.2). The assembler output is passed through tools/maspsx/maspsx.py to translate PsyQ syntax to GNU MIPS, then assembled by mips-linux-gnu-as. It is crucial to use mips-linux-gnu tools.

The project uses `splat` to carve `disc/SLUS_006.64` based on `config/slus_006.64.yaml` into `src/` (C) and `asm/` (assembly). `objdiff` verifies matches headlessly and outputs to `build/progress.json`.

heuristics.concept: PS1 Disc Format and Custom Overlays
heuristics.description: Standard disc images like `.mdf` often use 2448-byte sectors (with 96-byte padding). These must be stripped to 2352-byte standard `.bin` format using `tools/scripts/strip_mdf.py`. Xenogears stores its overlays (FIELD.BIN, MOVIE.BIN) inside custom LZSS compressed CD sectors, which cannot be seen via standard ISO 9660. The repository provides `tools/scripts/extract_overlays.py` to carve these directly from `Xenogears.bin`.

patterns.description: Example: If the compiler uses v0 instead of s0, try assigning the struct pointer to a volatile local variable before the loop.
